$comment: Contracts are the main gold faucet and the reason to plan a supply chain. Failing one costs the payout and some reputation, and nothing else.
$deadlineComment: Deadlines are stored as remaining time and only tick while the player is present, so real life never costs a contract.
$palateComment: What a faction actually drinks. Contracts used to be one hand-authored template per recipe, so 63 of 71 recipes were never asked for by anyone and the back half of the recipe book was decoration. A faction now has a PALATE — an essence direction — and commissions whatever discovered recipe sits closest to it, which means every recipe the player finds becomes something somebody wants. spreadDeg is how catholic the taste is: the widest angle from the palate that faction will still commission.

factions.$comment: Soldiers on campaign. Hardy, practical, drunk in the field.
Forge and hearth — the guild buys heat.
Stillness, breath and clear water. The temple will not touch shadow.
Night work, discreetly paid for. The narrowest palate and the deepest purse.

$derivedComment: Commissions generated from a faction's palate rather than from a template. Only DISCOVERED recipes are eligible — a contract you cannot possibly fill is a taunt, not a goal, and the authored templates below already do the job of pointing at recipes you have not met yet. derivedShare is how much of the board is generated; the rest stays hand-authored, so the signature orders keep showing up.

derived.$gradeComment: The floor rises with rank: an established shop is expected to deliver better work, and this is the only place the difficulty of a contract scales.
derived.$quantityComment: Cheap potions are ordered by the crate, expensive ones by the pair. Scaled off base value so a new recipe slots into the curve without being tuned by hand.
derived.$requirementComment: How often a derived order carries a vessel or seal condition. Kept low: the constraint is a spike of difficulty, and every order having one turns it into a tax.

templates.$comment: Plain water in quantity. A big, undemanding order, which is what a stacking vessel is actually for.
The deepest order in the game: pure Umbra means the shaft is fully beamed, and the amphora keeps the count sane.
